note: State compliance layer for a Cognition.X deployment — the registrations, agreements, checks and filings an adopting program office meets in each state, with the forms, agencies and fees as commonly published. THIS IS NOT LEGAL ADVICE and every figure is flagged verify: fees, forms and thresholds change yearly and the file records them as of the asOf year; confirm each with the named agency (or counsel) before filing. Nothing here asserts that Cognition.X is approved, registered or listed anywhere. The platform's own facts hold: nothing leaves a page on its own; simulation ≠ certification; access profiles are chosen supports, never diagnoses.
disclaimer: Not legal advice. Verify with the named agency before filing. Fees as of 2025.

federal: FERPA (34 CFR Part 99) — student education records; the 'school official' exception governs any vendor a school lets touch records
COPPA (16 CFR Part 312) — under-13 online data collection; a page that collects nothing on a server has nothing to send, but any hosted instance must comply
PPRA — surveys and evaluations touching protected topics
Section 504 / ADA Title II — accessibility of school technology (see accessibility)
privacy.platform: Cognition.X stores learner records only in the browser of the device in use; nothing leaves a page on its own and export is a deliberate act. That removes the server-side data flow most state operator laws regulate, but it does not remove the school's own duty: where a state requires a written data privacy agreement with any vendor or 'operator', sign one (the SDPC National Data Privacy Agreement with the state exhibit is the common instrument), and any hosted or synced deployment is a new review.

background.note: Every state fingerprints school employees; contractors and volunteers with unsupervised access to minors are covered by state law and district policy in varying ways. Assessors who witness checks in a school are, at minimum, subject to the district's volunteer/contractor policy. Typical cost per person: state + FBI fingerprint fee.

typical_cost.note: state BCI/DOJ fee + FBI fee; some districts bill through a vendor (Fieldprint, IdentoGO)

mandated.note: Every state has a mandated-reporter law; teachers and school staff are mandated reporters everywhere. Some states make every adult a mandated reporter ('universal'); several require training for school personnel. Training is usually free and online through the state child-welfare agency.

apprenticeship.note: Registered Apprenticeship programs are registered either with the federal Office of Apprenticeship (OA) or a DOL-recognized State Apprenticeship Agency (SAA). Registration is free. Cognition.X trade tracks are pre-apprenticeship curriculum: simulation ≠ certification, and a registered program's sponsor (the hall, the employer) holds the standards.
apprenticeship.federal: 29 CFR Part 29 (standards) and Part 30 (EEO in apprenticeship)

accessibility.note: The 2024 ADA Title II web rule (28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H) requires state and local government web content and mobile apps — public schools included — to meet WCAG 2.1 AA: by April 24, 2026 for entities serving 50,000+ people, April 26, 2027 for smaller ones. Section 508 applies to federal funds recipients' procurement in many states' own policies.
accessibility.platform: Every app carries skip links, lang, aria labels, live regions, keyboard operation and reduced-motion support (v0.33.0 first pass; v0.46.0 contrast verified ≥ 4.5:1). A full WCAG 2.2 AA audit is the open roadmap item — budget an external audit before a public-entity procurement.

nonprofit.note: A nonprofit organized in one state that runs programs, hires, or holds property in another usually must register there as a foreign nonprofit corporation (certificate of authority) with the Secretary of State, keep a registered agent in that state, and file an annual or biennial report. Merely licensing software or shipping a USB stick generally does not trigger it; running a cohort with staff on the ground usually does — ask counsel for the line in each state.

registered_agent.note: commercial registered agent, if no in-state address

charity.note: About 40 states require a nonprofit that solicits contributions from their residents to register before asking (and to renew annually, often with the Form 990). Online donation pages reachable from a state can count as soliciting in it (the Charleston Principles). Fees are small; the labor is the calendar.
charity.instrument: Unified Registration Statement (URS) is accepted by most registration states; several require their own form.

sales_tax.note: Nonprofit purchases are exempt from sales tax in some states on application, in others not at all; five states levy no state sales tax. Matters for devices and materials bought in-state.

cte.note: Each state education agency keeps a list of approved industry-recognized credentials that count toward CTE accountability and graduation pathways. Cognition.X credentials are practice records, not industry certifications; the path onto a state list is an application by the credential's owner in the state's annual window, and it is not assumed here.
